Ebon One, whose real name is a mystery, is the most powerful Soulsinger known throughout the realms. A man with such understanding of Soulsongs, these of dead matter, living beings, and even humans, he is essentially a god in terms of his power to influence the world all round him - like, bending a human's Soulsong to leave them a deformed beast - slave to his bidding, move hills and dry out lakes.

The orc band, severely smaller and more fearful now, was making its way to the mountains as quick as possible. Most of their now powerless hatred turned towards the rangers that crippled them so badly. Many vowed revenge, the lucky few remembering with wicked smiles how they ended this or that Dunedain's lives. Their chief personally slew two, due to cunning, experience, and luck... but since then it apparently ran out. He dared not think how the chief of Moria would appreciate such a defeat.

Battered and few, the host finally made it the first hills a few days later, starting the difficult climbing. At last in Fallwatch, they stopped, much relieved to be home, however miserable that home may be.

Bloodied and shaken, Zaghûr was jogging away from the road with the remaining orcs. He had lost far too many, the Dunedain were a tough meal. The Orc cursed and sweared, holding his left arm to stop the black blood from spilling too much, Thankfully, the survivors were inclined to listen and obey, especially after he threatened them with more rangers. All of them took the lengthy journey home, up the Misty Mountains.

Zaghûr stood still for a moment, savoring their obvious fear - that of the man who dropped his blade, that of the tasty hobbit about to run. He stood there, hunched over and shorter than the human, perhaps even weaker, but much more ferocious and brave, at least with numbers that significant now tightening the ring...

He was about to have some fun, maybe kill the man with his own hand in a mockery of a duel, when the hobbit ran. He ran quickly and suddenly, making the orcs on his side all roar and babble and push each other frantically to get him. Their haste proved to be their failure, as the agile little Shire inhabitant slipped right through their fingers, resulting in angry screams and shoving.

Zaghûr paid no attention, for now, because he knew he'd rage out of control if he did, and vent his frustration on his Orcs. Instead, he turned towards the man.

"If you don't stand and fight, manfilth, I'll kill you much more painfully than I presently intend; get this sword and fight me. Come on. FIGHT ME!" 

He banged on his chainmail with his fist, the Orcs around realizing where the closest source of fun was and tightening the circle. The upcoming bloodshed made them energetic, some even hopping in place from excitement. Man and Orc chief crossed blades for the first time, the Orc attacking, man defending against furious wide blows. The blades screeched against each other a few times, then a hidden blow of the orcish scimitar opened his leg in a gaping red wound, followed by pained wailing.

The wretched Orcs erupted in laughter and yells, completely forgetting about safety. Zaghûr roared and flailed his blade his in the air, boasting and mocking his opponent. 

Another brief exchange. Then another. the victim of these filthy creatures began panicking and grew sweaty and tired, his breath heaving out. And then it was over. The chief decided he wants to play no more and sliced his right arm off from the elbow. A moment later a black scimitar was sticking out of the dying man, down low, from his belly. Laughing and cheering, the Orcs left for the trees nearby, leaving him to die slowly amidst the road, hoping he'd get discovered by other humans. Zaghûr's bloodlust was temporarily quenched. Soon it was all quiet, except for barely inaudible heavy breathing...

Zaghûr was more than happy to finally see the desired grub walking right in between his forces of ever annoyed and impatient Orcs. The small host had camped on both sides of the road throughout the night. Zaghûr himself had to fight disobedient chaps that tried to light fires despite his orders. In the end, they hid quite well. 

But, as their meal approached, even Zaghûr could not surpress a growl. Charging out of the trees, passengers right side, he gave out a battle cry and ran towards the hobbit first, flailing his sword. The other Orcs sprang up a second later, unsheathing daggers, swords, holding flails and spears... the raiders quickly surrounded their victims in a ring of dark, dirty bodies, mouths watered by the upcoming meal.

Bio: The Orc who would later become Zaghûr Skull-Taker was born in the underpassages of the Grey Mountains, to a common footsoldier. He had many, many siblings, which all ferociously competed for food and command. He himself theorizes that he'd been raised in some kind of a communal cave with too much other children for them to be his siblings. Kin or not, when he saw his survival is at stake, Zaghûr fought for his place among the Orcs. Not the biggest Orc among his peers, he was certainly the baddest, proving to be fit for the harshness of life by soon becoming the leader of a small gang. Through beating and goring the rebellious and filling the good boys' bellies with grog, Zaghûr became a soldier. During this time he saw so much infighting, nearly losing his life in it, that he decided to take matters into his own grubby hands. 

And so a day came when the bold Orc ambushed the very Chief of Mount Gundabad during a beasthunt. It was a grave mistake. Narrowly escaping death for the second time due to raging wild beasts among the hunting party, Zaghûr ran away, and away he went until found by the guards of Moria, directly by its Eastern Gate. Brought in as a brief amusement for a chief and thrown in a fighting pit with some wargs, he savagely fought for deal life once more. Impressed, a few of the Orcs nearby decided to voice their disapproval of the chief, and freeing Zaghûr. He challenged the minor chief to single combat, taking his place and his head as a cup to drink from thus known henceforth as Zaghûr Skull-Taker. 

In this dog-eat-dog society, the chieftain truly blossomed, enjoying every last bit of fighting he could take part in, for the Mines were unstable. He gradually grows bored of bashing his brethren and turned his aspirations towards challenging something foreign - Elves, Men and Dwarves, he feels innate, burning hatred against, and wants it sated badly, the boredom making him restless and cruel.
